correctness.rationale: Fourier transform of a Gaussian derivative reduces nonzero STFT zeros to roots of F(u)=lambda+n log|(u−1)/(u+1)|+2cu, u=xi/omega not ±1, and exactly one time phase per real root modulo pi/omega. F′=2c+2n/(u²−1) is positive on each exterior interval, giving one root each. On (−1,1) the only extrema for c>n are ±v=sqrt(1−n/c), with extremal values lambda±H_n(c); hence 1, 2 (with double), or 3 internal distinct roots. The Jacobian at simple roots has index −sign F′, yielding conserved signed sum −1. The cubic expansion F=lambda+2(c−n)u−(2n/3)u³+O(u⁵) gives the unique cusp and 2/3 threshold law; F″ nonzero at noncusp folds. No extra zeros at xi=±omega.
residual_risks: For complex tone amplitudes the phase location shifts but the modulus root classification is unchanged.
The local topological degree is an index of the complex STFT, not of its squared magnitude; no generic multimode stability theorem.
